subject: Generation of annotation for custom/unknown cel/cdfs

messages.author: 2a04dc7fbb3e23f3
messages.subject: Generation of annotation for custom/unknown cel/cdfs
parts:
I apologize if this question has been asked before and I missed it in
the forums:

How would one go about 'creating' the UFL and UGP files for a cdf/cel
file collection from scratch? I have a set of files I am at that were
left by a previous student without any of this type of information. I
believe that there is a way to generate the UFL/UGP (and probably any
other annotation files) using the NetAffx and/or Fusion SDKs as
implemented here. Essentially, the CDF contains only an
'uninformative' set of probeset names such as

mm33-3-114836480 (organismBUILD - Chr - pos)

Could someone point me in the right direction?

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Generation of annotation for custom/unknown cel/cdfs
parts:
On Tue, Nov 25, 2008 at 10:56 AM, David Rosenberg
<david.m....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I apologize if this question has been asked before and I missed it in
> the forums:
>
> How would one go about 'creating' the UFL and UGP files for a cdf/cel
> file collection from scratch? I have a set of files I am at that were
> left by a previous student without any of this type of information. I
> believe that there is a way to generate the UFL/UGP (and probably any
> other annotation files) using the NetAffx and/or Fusion SDKs as
> implemented here. Essentially, the CDF contains only an
> 'uninformative' set of probeset names such as
>
> mm33-3-114836480 (organismBUILD - Chr - pos)
>
> Could someone point me in the right direction?

The UGP and UFL files are handled by the AromaUgpFile and the
AromaUflFile classes which are both subclasses of the
AromaTabularBinaryFile which always defines the underlying binary file
format (see http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/aromatabularbinaryfile).

See Page 'Aroma Unit Genome Position (UGP) files'
(http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/unit-genome-position-ugp-files)
for examples how to import NetAffx CSV data or other data to UGP files
or manually assign the values. Note that the records of an UGP file
(and also an UFL file) are indexed by units, that is, each row maps to
the corresponding unit (with the same index) in the CDF. Since your
unit names (we avoid the term probeset because a unit can contain
multiple groups/sets of probes) have format
<organismBUILD>-<chromosome>-<position> you can infer the (unit,
chromosome, position) from the unit names alone, in case you don't
have an NetAffx CSV file. For example:

unitNames <- getUnitNames(cdf);
pattern <- "(.*)-(.*)-(.*)";
chr <- gsub(pattern, "\\2", unitNames);
pos <- gsub(pattern, "\\3", unitNames);

chr <- as.integer(chr); # If there are 'X' and 'Y' you have to deal
with those too.
pos <- as.integer(pos);

Then, allocate an empty UGP file and assign (chr, pos) to it:

ugp <- AromaUgpFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="mm33,DM20081126");
ugp[,1] <- chr;
ugp[,2] <- pos;

That should do.

You can do similar things for your UFL file. See Page 'Unit Fragment
Length (UFL) files'
(http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/unit-fragment-length-ufl-files)
for further details.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Generation of annotation for custom/unknown cel/cdfs
parts:
On Wed, Nov 26, 2008 at 2:08 PM, David Rosenberg
<david.m....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thank you much for your help. A couple of follow-ups:
> 1. In terms of 'x', 'y' and 'other' chromosomes (and positions), should I
> just assign 'dummy' values? Should any be left NA?

For the human genome, I map ChrX=23 and ChrY=24. This seems to be the
de facto standard. For mitochondrial DNA, I've assigned it ChrM=25.
I don't know of a standard for this.

It is ok to have NAs, that is, for those units you cannot map
estimates to the genome. They will not show up in the
ChromosomeExplorer and they will not be part of any segmentation
either and so.
> 2. Lacking a NetAffx csv file, how might I determine fragment lengths?

I have no aces for this. If you know the restriction enzymes used,
you can find out at what locations they digest the DNA. This
information will define the lengths of all digested fragments. Then
you have to map the units in your CDF to these fragments. I haven't
done this myself and you will have to turn to external resources for
identifying the locations etc.

You could also try to contact Affymetrix to see if they have this
information for your custom CDF.

Cheers

/Henrik
